title: SLI: split streaming latency into TTFT vs stream duration + update SLO dashboards
author: Aisha Bello
release_notes: Streaming latency SLI is now computed from two indicators (TTFT + stream duration) instead of a single end-to-end metric; dashboards updated to show both. This improves burn-rate signal quality for streaming endpoints and reduces false budget burn driven by long generations.
body:
Context: Our current latency SLI for streaming endpoints (chat/completions w/ SSE) is effectively end-to-end request duration. That makes the SLI extremely sensitive to customer prompt/output length and customer-side stop behavior, and it obscures the reliability signal we actually care about (service responsiveness). This PR updates the SLI computation so streaming endpoints report and evaluate two latency indicators: (1) TTFT (time-to-first-token) and (2) stream duration (server-side time from first token to final token). We then update the Hosted tier latency SLI to use TTFT as the primary latency indicator and keep stream duration as a secondary/diagnostic indicator (visible in dashboards and alerts, but not gating budgets by default). Dedicated tier dashboards also get the new panels, but SLO policy remains unchanged in this PR.

What changed: 1) Metrics: add/standardize two histograms emitted from the API gateway for streaming routes: ttft_seconds and stream_duration_seconds. Both are recorded only for server-initiated successful streams (i.e. we exclude client aborts and auth/validation failures). 2) SLI computation: the SLO calc job now computes p95/p99 for TTFT separately from stream duration. The existing streaming latency SLI is renamed in code to make the semantics explicit, and the budget computation is wired to TTFT for Hosted. 3) Dashboards: update the standard SLO dashboard templates to show (a) TTFT p50/p95/p99, (b) stream duration p50/p95/p99, and (c) a small panel overlay showing request token counts to help interpret duration shifts. 4) Alert annotations: burn-rate alerts now include both TTFT and duration values in the alert payload for faster triage.

Key design choices: - TTFT is the SLO-carrying indicator for streaming endpoints because it best reflects perceived responsiveness and is less coupled to generation length. - Stream duration remains important for capacity issues / overload (e.g. very slow tokens/sec), but should not burn budgets when customers request long generations. We still want it visible and alertable, but tuned separately. - Exclusions: we explicitly exclude client aborts (HTTP 499 and gateway-disconnect class) from TTFT/duration latency distributions to avoid skew and to align with the streaming disconnect SLI work (see linked PRs / ENG-2428).

Implementation notes: - We rely on gateway timing hooks: ttft is measured from request accepted -> first SSE data frame written; stream_duration is measured from first SSE frame -> final frame / stream close initiated by server. - We use histogram buckets aligned with our standard latency buckets (ms-scale up to 60s) but TTFT uses tighter buckets in the low range. - Cardinality: metrics are labeled by tier, region, route_group, model_family (not raw model), and status_class. Route_group is one of: chat_stream, completions_stream. This is consistent with the cardinality budget proposal and avoids per-model explosions.

Example (PromQL-ish) used by the calc job: TTFT p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tier, region, route_group) (rate(redwood_gateway_stream_ttft_seconds_bucket{status_class="success"}[5m]))) Stream duration p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tier, region, route_group) (rate(redwood_gateway_stream_duration_seconds_bucket{status_class="success"}[5m])))

Testing/validation: - Backtested on 7d logs/metrics in us-east-1 + eu-west-1: TTFT distribution is stable across token counts while duration correlates strongly with completion length (expected). - Validated that client aborts no longer contaminate TTFT: compared 499-heavy periods from SUP-3924 reproduction, the TTFT p95 no longer spikes when clients disconnect mid-stream. - Added unit tests for the SLI aggregation logic and a small golden test for the dashboard JSON generation.

Rollout plan: - Land behind feature flag (sli.streaming_latency_split_enabled) for Hosted only; dashboards can show both immediately because they read both metrics when present. - After 48h of metric availability and query validation, flip the flag for all Hosted regions. Dedicated will follow after we confirm no per-customer labeling issues.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Consider a Dedicated-specific secondary SLO for tokens/sec (derived from duration + output_tokens) once we have consistent token counting across runtime/gateway. - Update the Confluence SLI spec with the exact classification/exclusion rules (ENG-2418 + ENG-2428).

Links: - Linear: ENG-2418 (Hosted tier SLIs), ENG-2425 (dashboards), ENG-2428 (streaming disconnect classification) - Related PRs: #18440 (disconnect classification), #18433 (tier propagation), #18470 (cardinality reduction)
commits: gateway: emit stream_ttft_seconds + stream_duration_seconds histograms for streaming routes
slo-calc: compute streaming TTFT p95/p99 separately from duration; wire Hosted latency SLI to TTFT
dashboards: add TTFT/duration panels + token count overlay; update naming + links to runbook
alerts: include TTFT/duration context in burn-rate alert annotations
tests: add aggregation unit tests + dashboard golden snapshots
ci_checks: slo-calc-integration: pass (rerun once after flaky test)
review_conversation: Allison Grant (requested changes): Can we be explicit in code/comments that TTFT is the SLO-carrying metric for Hosted? Also please confirm we’re excluding 499/client abort in BOTH TTFT and duration histograms, otherwise duration will still get skewed and confuse oncall.

Aisha Bello (author): Yep—updated variable names + added a comment in slo_calc indicating Hosted streaming latency SLI maps to TTFT. Also tightened exclusion filters so status_class=success only; client aborts are excluded in both histograms.

Nadia Rahman (requested changes): Bucket layout: TTFT buckets look too coarse below 250ms; we’ll lose resolution for p95 in good regions. Suggest adding 25/50/75/100/150/200ms buckets. Also please sanity check that model_family label is used (not model) to keep cardinality under control.

Aisha Bello (author): Added finer low-end buckets for TTFT and confirmed we only label by model_family. I also added a quick cardinality unit test to ensure model is not present in the emitted labelset.

Amara Diallo (comment): Gateway timing hooks look good. One edge case: when the request is accepted but the first write fails (e.g., upstream runtime 5xx before any token), TTFT should not record a duration. I think your code currently records a TTFT of ~0 if first write never happens.
Aisha Bello (author): Good catch. Updated to only observe TTFT on first successful SSE frame write. Added a test for ‘no first token’ path (runtime errors before streaming begins).
Thomas Baird (comment): Thanks for keeping labels tight. For route_group, please ensure we use a small fixed enum; do not include raw path.
Aisha Bello (author): Confirmed—route_group is hardcoded to chat_stream/completions_stream. No raw path labels.
Sergio Costa (approval): Dashboard updates look good. Love the token overlay. Approved once the doc link points to the new internal page (you have an old slug).
Aisha Bello (author): Updated doc link and re-rendered dashboards. Pushed final commit.
Allison Grant (approval): Approved. This should materially reduce false latency budget burns on long generations.
post_merge_notes: Deployed to staging immediately after merge; production rollout scheduled with feature flag default-off. Oncall playbook note added: when TTFT is healthy but duration is high, investigate tokens/sec + runtime saturation before declaring user-visible latency regression.
